The post Infini-AI-Lab Releases Hermit, an Open-Source Harness Adapter Framework for AI Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Infini-AI-Lab has released Hermit , an open-source harness adapter framework for AI agents. Hermit is a framework from Infini-AI-Lab that trains an external ‘harness adapter’ while the agent’s model and harness stay frozen. The first release, v0.1.0 , shipped on October 25, 2026. CMU postdoc Haizhong Zheng announced it on X on October 27. For developers, the pitch is simple: adapt Codex or Claude Code agents to new tasks without fine-tuning or forking the harness. TL;DR Footprint: A Python framework. No parameters of its own. Apache-2.0, pip install hermit-harness . Runs on: The offline Quick Start needs no GPU, model account or dataset. Real runs use any API backend or a local vLLM, SGLang or Ollama server. Performance: Reported gains over no-adapter baselines on OfficeQA, CL-Bench and ServeLearnBench, all with GLM 5.3 Flash. Best: MWM adapter hits 0.795 accuracy on CL-Bench database exploration, vs 0.580 for the in-context baseline. Worst: The prompt-only adapter scores 0.470 on the same venue, below that 0.580 baseline. Bottom line: Best: one training loop for 5 harness evolution methods. Worst: most results are single runs, self-reported. What is a harness adapter? A harness adapter is a trainable external harness. It works like a plugin with training support built in. A model adapter, such as LoRA, adapts a model. A harness adapter adapts an existing agent instead. The adapter can hold instructions, skills, memory, tools, executable code and agent coordination logic. It can even be a whole repository. Its specification says which parts are learnable and how updates get checked. The base model and harness never change. The team gives 3 reasons for this design. Many harnesses are closed-source. Editing open ones can break carefully tuned component interactions. And a learned adapter can move between compatible models and harnesses. How does Hermit train an adapter? Hermit uses an RL-style training loop . A Trainer runs a batch of tasks through the acting agent with the current adapter. A judge scores the outputs. An Evolver reads the trajectories and feedback, then proposes a new adapter. The Trainer checks it against the template and commits it as the next version. Every adapter version lives in a git tree. You can inspect, roll back or ship any version. Learner programs can run sandboxed, which requires Linux with bubblewrap. Five evolution methods ship today: GEPA , SkillOpt , MetaWorld Model (MWM), Harness² and Continual Harness . ACE and ReHarness are listed as coming soon. You can also write your own Evolver.
